conformance.note: A non-empty `undispatchable` means the capability table names a verb dispatch cannot reach -- the published guard surface would be describing protection over nothing.

accepts: a relative path within the project
an absolute directory the host grants (an existing directory holding .git, .gm, package.json, Cargo.toml, go.mod or pyproject.toml)
an absolute path outside the project root with no ".." segment
read_outside_root_opt_in.note: The opt-in widens WHICH root a read may address, never whether a read may climb out of one. It is per call and never inferred from the path shape, so a call without it fails exactly as before.
requires: the literal boolean body field "allowOutsideRoot": true on that same call
"allow_outside_root" and "allowAbsolute" are aliases; a non-boolean value is not an opt-in
still_rejected: any ".." segment, with or without the opt-in
every write verb: fs_write stays project-only and ignores the flag

unguarded.note: These reach the network and a Node process with no allowlist of their own. That is deliberate -- they exist to run arbitrary caller-supplied work -- but it means the trust boundary for them is the CALLER, not this layer.

persisted_paths.note: these paths are a compatibility surface -- a reader outside this crate depends on each staying where it is

shared_store_contract.aggregate_hazard: an UNFILTERED aggregate over an F32_BLOB vector table answers 0 even when the table is full. Count with a predicate, or with SUM over a GROUP BY subquery, or against the <table>_vec_shadow companion. A bare COUNT(*) reporting 0 is not evidence of an empty store.
shared_store_contract.busy_timeout_ceiling_rule: must stay well under the host dispatch deadline (120s). A wait that outlives the epoch budget TRAPS the instance instead of returning a reportable SQLITE_BUSY, and a trap carries no error text -- contention then looks like a crash.
shared_store_contract.identity: the resolved file path IS the identity -- libsql routes by path alone and ignores the `db` handle name for any real file (that field is consulted only for :memory:), so two callers naming the same file share one store and two projects with different files cannot collide
shared_store_contract.isolation: none beyond the path. There is no per-plugin namespace and no ownership claim; any plugin handed the path reaches the whole store, including tables another plugin created.
shared_store_contract.journal_mode: WAL where the conversion succeeds. It needs an exclusive lock, so it is attempted once per process per path and memoized only on a verified read-back -- PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL returns OK while silently doing nothing when it cannot take the lock.
shared_store_contract.locking: the WASI VFS has no OS file locking and serializes with a <db>.lock DIRECTORY. It is created before a write and removed after, so an unclean exit leaves it behind and every later write returns SQLITE_BUSY forever -- no holder to find, no timeout that expires it, survives reboots. A locked error now names the directory and the remedy.

effective_config.why: gm's own shared default config repo at https://github.com/AnEntrypoint/gm-config (no project or user config.source.json configured)

plugin_response_envelope.failure: {ok: false, error: string}; a missing `error` on a failed response is classified by plugin_failure_code

hazards.unfiltered_aggregate_on_vector_table: DRIVER-SPECIFIC, measured under node:sqlite and NOT reproducing through the agentplug-libsql wasm plugin (2026-08-02: bare COUNT(*) on rssearch_vectors answers 278 there, matching the predicated form exactly). Under node:sqlite an UNFILTERED aggregate over a libsql F32_BLOB vector table answers 0 even when the table is full. Measured on this repo's store: `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM rssearch_vectors` returns 0, and the subquery form without a WHERE also returns 0 -- but the same aggregate WITH any predicate returns 755, reconciling exactly against 428 live plus 327 tombstoned rows. The missing predicate is the trigger, not the aggregate. The query verbs pass SQL through untouched, so nothing stops a caller reading that 0 as an empty knowledgebase and acting on it (dropping the table, re-indexing, reporting data loss). Always count with a predicate, or count the <table>_vec_shadow companion. PRAGMA integrity_check is separately unreliable on these tables -- it fails with `unknown function: libsql_vector_idx()`, which is not corruption.

payload_field_by_verb.bert.embed: embedding (plus `dim`); takes {text, kind} where kind="query" selects the query conditioning, anything else is treated as a passage
payload_field_by_verb.libsql.begin/commit/rollback: REFUSED -- there is no transaction: each exec/query is its own cycle. The plugin answers ok:false naming the unsupported verb.
payload_field_by_verb.libsql.list_dbs: dbs (always empty: connections are no longer tracked by name)
payload_field_by_verb.libsql.open/close: ACCEPTED BUT INERT -- every exec/query is its own open-operate-close cycle, so these are no-ops kept only so existing callers do not break.
payload_field_by_verb.libsql.serialize: bytes_b64 (also mirrored as `data` for older callers; `bytes_b64` is the contract field)
payload_field_by_verb.treesitter.lang_for_ext: lang (null when the extension is unrecognized)
payload_field_by_verb.treesitter.parse: nodes (plus `lang`, null when neither ext nor lang resolves -- an unresolved language is ok:true with an empty nodes array, NOT an error)

plugin_response_envelope.shape: flat: {ok: bool, <payload-field>: ...} -- NOT wrapped under `data` the way a gm verb response is

codesearch.note: not run: the probe is a real codesearch, measured at 40-160s on a large project, which no dispatch caller's timeout survives. Pass {"probes": true} to run it.
